record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Lovasz induced path with connected complement
record.original_question: For every natural number l at least 3, does there exist an integer f(l) such that for any two vertices x and y in any f(l)-connected graph G, there is an induced path P from x to y for which the vertex-deleted graph G - V(P) is l-connected?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3[63] For each natural number l, there exists an integer f(l) such that, for any two vertices x and y in an f(l)-connected graph G, there exists an induced xy-path P such that G − V (P) is l-connected.
It is easy to verify that f(1) = 3 by Tutte’s wheel theorem. Kriesell[38] and Chen et al.[19] independently proved that f(2) = 5. For k ≥ 3, f(k) is not known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph G is k-connected if it has more than k vertices and remains connected after the deletion of any fewer than k vertices. An induced path in G is a path P such that the subgraph of G induced by V(P) is exactly P (i.e., no chords). For a subgraph H of G, let G - V(H) denote the graph obtained from G by deleting the vertices of H together with all incident edges.

Prove or disprove: for every integer l ≥ 3, there exists an integer f(l) such that for every f(l)-connected graph G and every pair of distinct vertices x, y of G, there exists an induced x–y path P in G for which G - V(P) is l-connected.

(It is known that such an f exists with f(1) = 3 and f(2) = 5; the question concerns all l ≥ 3.)
artifact.status_search_result: The induced-path removal conjecture of Lovász/Kriesell is verified for l = 1 (Tutte's wheel theorem) and l = 2 (Kriesell; Chen et al.). For l ≥ 3 the existence of f(l) remains open. A non-induced weakening was established by Kawarabayashi–Reed–Wollan, and an induced-cycle variant has been proved, but the induced-path statement is still listed as open (e.g., on the Open Problem Garden).

status_evidence.title: Lovász Path Removal Conjecture | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: there exists f(k) such that for every f(k)-connected graph G and pair u,v, there is a u-v path P with G - V(P) k-connected.
status_evidence.claim: The path removal conjecture is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A weaker version of Lovász' path removal conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Kawarabayashi, Reed, Wollan prove a weakening (not requiring P to be induced) with f(k)=1600k^4+k+2.
status_evidence.claim: Only a non-induced weaker version has been established; the induced version remains open for l ≥ 3.
